passages.text: In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord seated on a throne, high and exalted; and the train of His robe filled the temple.
passages.sermon:
King Uzziah died that year.
I saw the Lord.
The Lord sat on a throne.
The throne was high.
The throne was exalted.
The Lord’s robe had a train.
The train of His robe filled the temple.
passages.original: בִּשְׁנַת־ מוֹת֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ עֻזִּיָּ֔הוּ וָאֶרְאֶ֧ה אֶת־ אֲדֹנָ֛י יֹשֵׁ֥ב עַל־ כִּסֵּ֖א רָ֣ם וְנִשָּׂ֑א וְשׁוּלָ֖יו מְלֵאִ֥ים אֶת־ הַהֵיכָֽל׃

passages.text: Above Him stood seraphim, each having six wings: With two wings they covered their faces, with two they covered their feet, and with two they were flying.
passages.sermon:
Seraphim are heavenly beings.
They stood above the Lord.
Each seraph had six wings.
With two wings, each seraph covered its face.
With two wings, each seraph covered its feet.
With two wings, each seraph flew.
passages.original: שְׂרָפִ֨ים עֹמְדִ֤ים׀ מִמַּ֙עַל֙ ל֔וֹ שֵׁ֧שׁ כְּנָפַ֛יִם שֵׁ֥שׁ כְּנָפַ֖יִם לְאֶחָ֑ד בִּשְׁתַּ֣יִם׀ יְכַסֶּ֣ה פָנָ֗יו וּבִשְׁתַּ֛יִם יְכַסֶּ֥ה רַגְלָ֖יו וּבִשְׁתַּ֥יִם יְעוֹפֵֽף׃

passages.text: And they were calling out to one another: “Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of Hosts; all the earth is full of His glory.”
passages.sermon:
The seraphim stood above the Lord.
The seraphim called out to each other.
They said, "Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of Hosts."
The LORD of Hosts is completely holy.
All the earth is full of His glory.
passages.original: וְקָרָ֨א זֶ֤ה אֶל־ זֶה֙ וְאָמַ֔ר קָד֧וֹשׁ׀ קָד֛וֹשׁ קָד֖וֹשׁ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת מְלֹ֥א כָל־ הָאָ֖רֶץ כְּבוֹדֽוֹ׃

passages.text: At the sound of their voices the doorposts and thresholds shook, and the temple was filled with smoke.
passages.sermon:
The seraphim called out with loud voices.
Their voices made the doorposts shake.
Their voices made the thresholds tremble.
Smoke filled the temple.
passages.original: וַיָּנֻ֙עוּ֙ אַמּ֣וֹת הַסִּפִּ֔ים מִקּ֖וֹל הַקּוֹרֵ֑א וְהַבַּ֖יִת יִמָּלֵ֥א עָשָֽׁן׃

passages.text: Then I said: “Woe is me, for I am ruined, because I am a man of unclean lips dwelling among a people of unclean lips; for my eyes have seen the King, the LORD of Hosts.”
passages.sermon:
Isaiah was a prophet.
Isaiah saw the Lord of Hosts, who is the King.
Isaiah said, “Woe is me.”
Isaiah said, “I am ruined.”
Isaiah said, “I am a man with unclean lips.”
Isaiah said, “I live among a people with unclean lips.”
Isaiah said, “My eyes have seen the King, the LORD of Hosts.”
passages.original: וָאֹמַ֞ר אֽוֹי־ לִ֣י כִֽי־ נִדְמֵ֗יתִי כִּ֣י אִ֤ישׁ טְמֵֽא־ שְׂפָתַ֙יִם֙ אָנֹ֔כִי וּבְתוֹךְ֙ עַם־ טְמֵ֣א שְׂפָתַ֔יִם אָנֹכִ֖י יוֹשֵׁ֑ב כִּ֗י אֶת־ הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת רָא֥וּ עֵינָֽי׃

passages.text: Then one of the seraphim flew to me, and in his hand was a glowing coal that he had taken with tongs from the altar.
passages.sermon:
Isaiah saw a vision in the temple.
A seraph is a heavenly being with great holiness.
One seraph flew toward Isaiah.
The seraph held a burning coal in his hand.
The seraph had taken the coal from the altar.
The seraph used tongs to take the coal.
passages.original: וַיָּ֣עָף אֵלַ֗י אֶחָד֙ מִן־ הַשְּׂרָפִ֔ים וּבְיָד֖וֹ רִצְפָּ֑ה בְּמֶ֨לְקַחַ֔יִם לָקַ֖ח מֵעַ֥ל הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃

passages.text: And with it he touched my mouth and said: “Now that this has touched your lips, your iniquity is removed and your sin is atoned for.”
passages.sermon:
A seraph touched my mouth with a burning coal.
He spoke to me.
He said, “This coal has touched your lips.”
He said, “Your iniquity is taken away.”
He said, “Your sin is atoned for.”
passages.original: וַיַּגַּ֣ע עַל־ פִּ֔י וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הִנֵּ֛ה נָגַ֥ע זֶ֖ה עַל־ שְׂפָתֶ֑יךָ וְסָ֣ר עֲוֺנֶ֔ךָ וְחַטָּאתְךָ֖ תְּכֻפָּֽר׃

passages.text: Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying: “Whom shall I send? Who will go for Us?” And I said: “Here am I. Send me!”
passages.sermon:
The Lord spoke.
The Lord asked a question.
The Lord said, "Whom shall I send?"
The Lord also said, "Who will go for Us?"
I heard the Lord's voice.
I answered the Lord.
I said, "Here am I."
I said, "Send me."
passages.original: וָאֶשְׁמַ֞ע אֶת־ ק֤וֹל אֲדֹנָי֙ אֹמֵ֔ר אֶת־ מִ֥י אֶשְׁלַ֖ח וּמִ֣י יֵֽלֶךְ־ לָ֑נוּ וָאֹמַ֖ר הִנְנִ֥י שְׁלָחֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: And He replied: “Go and tell this people, ‘Be ever hearing, but never understanding; be ever seeing, but never perceiving.’
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Isaiah.
God gave Isaiah a command.
God said, "Go to this people."
God told Isaiah to deliver a message.
God said, "You will hear again and again."
God said, "But you will not understand."
God said, "You will see again and again."
God said, "But you will not perceive."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לֵ֥ךְ וְאָמַרְתָּ֖ לָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֑ה שִׁמְע֤וּ שָׁמ֙וֹעַ֙ וְאַל־ תָּבִ֔ינוּ וּרְא֥וּ רָא֖וֹ וְאַל־ תֵּדָֽעוּ׃

passages.text: Make the hearts of this people calloused; deafen their ears and close their eyes. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn and be healed.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Isaiah.
God gave Isaiah a command about the people of Israel.
God said, “Make the hearts of these people hard.
Make their hearts unable to feel.
Make their ears heavy so they cannot hear.
Shut their eyes so they cannot see.
If they could see with their eyes,
If they could hear with their ears,
If they could understand with their hearts,
They would turn back to Me.
I would heal them.”
passages.original: הַשְׁמֵן֙ לֵב־ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה וְאָזְנָ֥יו הַכְבֵּ֖ד וְעֵינָ֣יו הָשַׁ֑ע פֶּן־ יִרְאֶ֨ה בְעֵינָ֜יו וּבְאָזְנָ֣יו יִשְׁמָ֗ע וּלְבָב֥וֹ יָבִ֛ין וָשָׁ֖ב וְרָ֥פָא לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Then I asked: “How long, O Lord?” And He replied: “Until the cities lie ruined and without inhabitant, until the houses are left unoccupied and the land is desolate and ravaged, until the LORD has driven men far away and the land is utterly forsaken.
passages.sermon:
Isaiah was a prophet of God.
Isaiah spoke to the Lord.
Isaiah asked, "How long, O Lord?"
The Lord answered Isaiah.
The Lord said, "Cities will become ruined."
No one will live in the cities.
Houses will be empty.
No people will be in the houses.
The land will become desolate.
The land will be destroyed.
The Lord will drive people far away.
The land will be left utterly forsaken.
passages.original: וָאֹמַ֕ר עַד־ מָתַ֖י אֲדֹנָ֑י וַיֹּ֡אמֶר עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁר֩ אִם־ שָׁא֨וּ עָרִ֜ים מֵאֵ֣ין יוֹשֵׁ֗ב וּבָתִּים֙ מֵאֵ֣ין אָדָ֔ם וְהָאֲדָמָ֖ה תִּשָּׁאֶ֥ה שְׁמָמָֽה׃ וְרִחַ֥ק יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־ הָאָדָ֑ם וְרַבָּ֥ה הָעֲזוּבָ֖ה בְּקֶ֥רֶב הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: And though a tenth remains in the land, it will be burned again. As the terebinth and oak leave stumps when felled, so the holy seed will be a stump in the land.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Isaiah.
God described what would happen to the people of Israel.
A small part of the people would remain in the land.
This part would be only a tenth of the people.
Even this tenth would face destruction again.
The land would not be spared from judgment.
When a terebinth tree is cut down, it leaves a stump.
When an oak tree is cut down, it also leaves a stump.
In the same way, a holy seed would remain in the land.
This holy seed would be like a stump left after the trees are cut down.
passages.original: וְע֥וֹד בָּהּ֙ עֲשִׂ֣רִיָּ֔ה וְשָׁ֖בָה וְהָיְתָ֣ה לְבָעֵ֑ר כָּאֵלָ֣ה וְכָאַלּ֗וֹן אֲשֶׁ֤ר בְּשַׁלֶּ֙כֶת֙ מַצֶּ֣בֶת בָּ֔ם זֶ֥רַע קֹ֖דֶשׁ מַצַּבְתָּֽהּ׃פ
